knowledge_gaps: A sampled-versus-full-catalog HR@10 gap is expected because candidate counts differ; it does not by itself establish defective discrimination. Define the diagnostic question and report eligible catalog size and rank percentile alongside ranks.

Five candidate draws give coarse hit frequencies and weak estimates of flip probability. Exact greater/tied counts permit analytical sampled-hit probabilities under uniform sampling without replacement, avoiding unnecessary rescoring.

Eligibility is ambiguous: excluding items in the truncated model input differs from excluding all preceding public training interactions. Specify the primary rule, record repeat targets, and keep the mandatory five-user/category unseen-item recommendation workflow intact.

The report does not specify popularity-bin boundaries, deterministic user ordering, bootstrap replicate count, paired aggregation formulas, or which layer aggregates category outputs. These details are needed for reproducibility; two supported users alone do not make bootstrap intervals reliable.

Matching precision does not guarantee chunk-invariant scores. Add target rescoring and chunk-size consistency checks, explicit tensor shapes, and finite-target validation before claiming exact numerical ranks.

The diagnostic remains in-sample and cannot distinguish memorization, shortcut learning, or generalization. Its connection to a subsequent HSTU improvement needs a predeclared decision rule; only host validation HR@10 can establish selection gains.

Originality 4 is reasonable. Potential 8 and difficulty 4 are provisional: usefulness depends on actionable findings, while unresolved mapping, routing, numerical consistency, and catalog cost may increase implementation difficulty. Full bibliographic details should replace the unnamed candidate-sampling reference.
